title: The full-degree vertex necessity conjecture for saturation of joins
statement:
Let $F$ be a non-empty graph and let $n\geq |V(F)|+1$. Write $K_1\vee F$ for the join of $F$ with a single vertex, and call a vertex **full-degree** if its degree is $n-1$. An **extremal graph** for saturation is an $n$-vertex $K_1\vee F$-saturated graph with $\operatorname{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)$ edges.

**Full-degree vertex necessity conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)=n-1+\operatorname{sat}(n-1,F),
$$

then some extremal graph of $K_1\vee F$ contains a full-degree vertex.

The conjecture proposes a necessary structural condition for equality in the standard upper bound obtained by adjoining a universal vertex to an extremal $F$-saturated graph. The paper's discussion shows that, for the particular join $K_1\vee(K_{p-1}^-\cup K_1)$, extremal graphs have no full-degree vertex, but it does not establish the conjecture in general.
source_name: Xinying Hua and Yuejian Peng, “Saturation numbers of some joins of graphs”, arXiv:2606.22006 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22006

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
